verdict.rationale: Elastic documents ad-hoc ES|QL queries, Discover search and filtering, and a columnar engine 'engineered for high-cardinality'. It also describes itself as schema-agnostic, which suggests ad-hoc slicing without pre-aggregation. However, no evidence shows grouping by arbitrary high-cardinality fields like user or request IDs without mappings or index setup, and the high-cardinality claim is framed around time series metrics. Missing for 10: explicit docs on GROUP BY/STATS over arbitrary high-cardinality event fields, confirmation that no index or mapping definition is needed, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can group and filter by high-cardinality fields (user id, request id) without pre-aggregating or defining indexes first

citations.quote: Elastic is built on a columnar time series database engineered for high-cardinality
Elastic is open by design, schema-agnostic
Use **Discover** to search, filter, and tail all your logs ingested into your project in one place.
